In the days before the 2020 election, a group of Donald Trump supporters
[surrounded](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2023/oct/01/trump-train-attack-
biden-bus-january-6) a Biden-Harris campaign bus in Texas, seemingly trying to
force it off the road.

"We love what they did, but here's the thing they don't know," Marco Rubio
[said](https://floridapolitics.com/archives/379803-we-do-that-in-florida-
every-day-marco-rubio-backs-texas-trump-train-despite-investigation/) shortly
after. "We do that in Florida every day."

It was one of several moments that revealed how the Florida senator was
changing.

"That was not who I thought I knew - who I always thought was really
respectful of democracy, and worked well with Democrats," a former Rubio
Senate staffer tells **Zeteo**. "Being flippant about some of these things
that either were, or were adjacent to, political violence… this crossed the
line, for me anyway."

Others saw something else.

"That's typical Marco Rubio, trying to get something positive out of it,
because he knows deep down that was wrong," Mike Fasano, a former Florida
state legislator who served alongside Rubio, says with a chuckle. "Marco Rubio
has still a great future in his political life - and I can understand why he
says some of the things he says, because I've seen firsthand how you get
elected. You have to appease the primary voter."

One of the most successful Republicans in the modern era, Rubio has
consistently meant different things to different people. He has climbed from a
state legislature, to the U.S. Senate, to one of the most powerful offices in
the world, leading the State Department in Trump's second administration.

Rubio rose on the strength of his backstory, the son of Cuban exiles. He was
seen as a conservative but reasonable Republican, a supporter of immigration
reform, free speech, human rights, and foreign aid as soft power. That's all
changed.

It is a feature of the Trump era that most Republicans have put aside supposed
morals and beliefs in order to maintain - or gain - power. Perhaps none have
debased themselves as conspicuously, thoroughly, and successfully as Rubio.
